en: "You have done splendidly in bringing the light back to the land."{w}{p}"With this, I believe we can rest easy, for the time being at least."{w}
"I shall grant you a reward."{w}

"Well done retaking the Palace of the Sun.{w}Look -- see how the land shines beneath the pouring sunlight."{w}{p}"You have done a great deal for us.{w}But perhaps this was something only adventurers could have accomplished."{w}{p}"...I am grateful.{w}The wait for your safe return felt long indeed."{w}{p}"Now then, let us leave the talk at that.{w}Follow me. It is time for the victory parade."{w}
note: Rianna (Roscadil's ruler, addressed as Your Majesty in slice_13) speaks in a clipped, imperial register throughout; no pronouns used for Rianna (glossary gender unknown).

en: "You did us a great service with the Palace of the Sun.{w}Peace should now come to the land as well.{w}...For a while, at least."{w}

Rianna looked away from you and gazed, squinting against the glare, at the sun shining beyond the window.{w}{p}Rianna's expression seemed filled with a clear sense of accomplishment, and yet somehow lonely.{w}
note: Name repeated instead of a pronoun (gender unknown).

en:
"How are you all faring?
No trouble since then?"{w}
"Balgert was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Algrantz at once."{w}
note: Source typo [JP] read as [JP] (go to).

en: "Fulgrant was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Ogre Bay at once."{w}
note: [JP] = Ogre Bay, as in pilot row 160 / slice_10 row 737.

en: "Someone from Perpeco Village was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Perpeco Forest at once."{w}
note: Same pattern as slice_10 rows 736-738.

en: "What is it? What's the matter... a package?{w}From Barjeff... a confidential parcel...?{w}...It's big."{w}{p}"Hmph. Well, very well.{w}You have come a long way. Thank you for your trouble.{w}...Now, I don't recall asking for anything..."{w}
note: The party is delivering the parcel from Barjeff (slice_18 row 1396: Barjeff, chief of Teridon, sends a secret parcel to Emperor Rianna).

en: "Blatantly suspicious.{w}I could just burn it as it is...{w}But I suppose I should check what's inside first... --!"{w}
note: Line cut off by a gasp ([JP]) as Barjeff pops out; kept interrupted.

en: Barjeff
note: New name [JP], romanized Barjeff (not in glossary). Chief ([JP]) of Teridon per slice_18. Gender unknown in glossary; no pronouns used.

en: "Riannaaa! I love youuu!{w}HUUUUUUUUGGGGGG!!!"{w}
"You insolent wretch!{w}What do you think you're doing!?"{w}

"W-wait wait wait wait wait!
Put the magic gun down, okay!?{w}No violence! Let's settle this with love, I say!"{w}
note: [JP] = "magic gun" (new term; cf. [JP] in slice_13).

en: "You're the one who laid hands on me first!{w}And now, of all times, you make excuses!?{w}What you have done deserves ten thousand deaths!!"{w}{p}"Now submit quietly and be cut down by my own hand, here and now!"{w}
note: [JP] = a lord personally executing an offender; rendered "cut down by my own hand".

en: "I told you to wait!{w}Ah, I see now -- you've been blinded by my love! It's me, Barjeff!"{w}{p}"You said it yourself before, didn't you!?{w}'Let's see you export this so-called love of yours!'{w}So here I am, doing just that--!"{w}
note: [JP] rendered with single quotes as a quoted remark. [JP] (old-fashioned) gives Barjeff a slightly pompous ring.

en: "...I know full well it's you.{w}Is that supposed to be a problem?"{w}
note: [JP] = she knows it is Barjeff and is going to punish anyway. Rendered as knowing who it is; could also be read as "I am well aware (of what I said)".

en: "So that you bring no shame on the name of Teridon,{w}I shall erase you without a trace.{w}
note: No closing quote in source; the next row repeats this text inside {0E}..{0F}. [JP] romanized Teridon (new place name, the TRD town).
{0E}..{0F} repeats row 1059 with {w} -> \n, as in source. [JP] = punishment shout, rendered "Perish!".

en: "I may die, but love is immortal!{w}
note: No closing quote in source; repeated in next row.

en:
{0E}"I may die, but love is immortal!{0F}
GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"{w}
"Ship this piece of garbage back to Teridon at once.{w}...Incidentally."{w}
"Don't tell me you knew about this farce and...{w}
note: No closing quote in source; repeated in next row. Line trails off deliberately.

en:
{0E}"Don't tell me you knew about this farce and...{0F}
...Heh. A foolish question.{w}Thank you for your trouble."{w}
note: [JP] left as ambiguous as the source (obviously knew / obviously did not).

en: "...I stayed true... to love...{w}My life... was a good one..."{w}{p}"...You adventurers... think so too... don't you?{w}Cherish... love..."{w}
"Slump."{w}
note: [JP] is spoken aloud (Barjeff voices his own collapse, a gag); rendered as a spoken sound word.

en:
Lumisthenes was nothing like its usual self.
The city had suddenly been attacked by the forces of darkness, and people were being set upon everywhere.{w}{p}The screams of panic-stricken people rang out from every direction.{w}{p}Among them, a familiar cry reached your ears.{w}
note: [JP] = "the forces of darkness" (new term).

en: Decoy
note: Glossary spelling.

en:
"Waaah!!
Stay the hell awaaaay!!"{w}

"A magic puppet, is it...
Hardly satisfying prey for the pleasure of taking a life... but no matter."{w}
note: [JP] = "magic puppet" (new term; what Decoy is).

en:
"Whoa whoa whoa, rethink this!!
You won't get nothin' tasty outta eatin' me-e-e!"{w}
note: Decoy uses rough [JP]/[JP] speech; rendered with dropped g's and slang.

en: Shaharon's dark hand reached out toward the cowering Decoy.{w}
With a flash of a white blade, a young swordswoman with a magnificent beard stepped in front of Shaharon, barring the way.{w}
note: [JP] = young (girl) swordswoman, stated by the source itself; no pronoun needed. This is Milonya (next name box).

en: Milonya
note: Glossary spelling.

en: "What do you think you're doing to my darling Decoykins!?!"{w}
note: [JP] -> "Decoykins" throughout (English diminutive for the doting [JP]; the project does not use -chan). Neighbouring slices (15, 16) should adopt the same.

en: "Decoykins, now that Milonya's here, everything's gonna be A-OK!"{w}
note: Milonya refers to herself by name ([JP]); kept. [JP] in katakana -> "A-OK".

en: "...Uh."{w}{p}"Th-thanks..."{w}
note: [JP] before [JP] read as a hesitant start; "Uh" + stammered "Th-thanks" keeps both readings.

en:
"S-so cuuute!
Aaah, I wanna make you my briiide!!"{w}
note: [JP]: want to take Decoy as a bride (gag on Milonya being the suitor). Read as addressed to Decoy; could be an aside.

en:
"Heh, what a racket...
But this may prove rather entertaining."{w}

"What?
This shadow..."{w}
A huge shadow fell over the entire city.{w}Looking up at the sky, you saw a silver dragon soaring serenely overhead.{w}
note: [JP] = "silver dragon".

en:
"So the primeval dragon would interfere...
I shall withdraw for now."{w}{p}"It seems your kind is presumptuously scheming to storm our stronghold, but it is futile."{w}{p}"After all, even the Moonlight Spirit wishes for us to take hold of the sun."{w}
note: The schemer in [JP] is unstated; rendered "your kind" (whoever stands before Shaharon: the party / Milonya / the townsfolk). [JP] = Moonlight Spirit (slice_02/05).

en: The forces of darkness vanished along with Shaharon, like a receding wave.{w}{p}As if it had been watching to see this through, the silver dragon flying overhead also rose up into a break in the clouds and passed from sight.{w}
Gradually, quiet returned to the city, and you headed to the Temple of Rafa.{w}
note: [JP] = Temple of Rafa (pilot row 1, slice_09).

en: You asked Natori about the dragon that had appeared in the sky over the city, and about the Moonlight Spirit Shaharon had mentioned before leaving.{w}

"A silver dragon?
One so mighty the monsters turned tail...{w}Oh! Maybe it's...!"{w}

"Could it be Agintaitus, the dragon of myth?
The legends do mention a silver dragon."{w}
note: New name [JP] romanized Agintaitus (possibly from Romanian argint "silver" -> Argintaitus; flagged). Also in slice_16 row 1231.

en:
"But it's a creature of myth, so I can't really say for sure."{w}{p}"And the Moonlight Spirit... I think that means Yorfa, who governs the moon, but I don't know much more than the name myself."{w}{p}"Sorry.
If I knew more, I'd love to tell you..."{w}
note: [JP]: honorific dropped ("Lady" would assume gender).

en:
"Hmm...
Oh! This is exactly when you should go ask Council Chair Wattner!"{w}{p}"The Chair just might know something."{w}
note: [JP] = Council Chair (slice_09 row 684). Subject of [JP] = the party (next row they go to Wattner).

en: You spoke to Wattner, who was busy handling the aftermath at the Central Council.{w}
note: [JP] = Central Council (new term).

en:
"A giant silver dragon, you say...
Then it is almost certainly the great dragon Agintaitus."{w}{p}"I have heard that it is the guardian of a place called the Castle of the Wind, which has floated in the sky since ancient times. They say it has watched over this world since time long past."{w}{p}"As for the Castle of the Wind, you would do better to ask Mayleen at the Observatory than me."{w}
note: [JP] = Castle of the Wind, [JP] = Observatory (new terms).

en: You asked Wattner to tell you about Yorfa, the Moonlight Spirit, as well.{w}

"Yorfa, the Moonlight Spirit?
...Well now, I'm afraid I don't know."{w}
note: [JP] may be evasive (next row: nothing more could be gotten out of Wattner); "Well now" keeps that hint without stating it.

en:
It seemed you would get nothing more out of Wattner.
You headed to the Observatory.{w}

"The Castle of the Wind, where the ancient dragon Agintaitus dwells?
That castle floats inside a great thundercloud, so there is no way to get there."{w}{p}"I hear the elven nation is building a ship that flies through the sky, but they would never lend it out for a mere survey."{w}
note: [JP] = "the elven nation" (presumably Rianna's Roscadil; left unnamed as in source). Mayleen keeps her refined register.

en: "...Well, if you were swept up in a tornado or some such and lucky enough to land there, that would be another matter..."{w}
A storm blew in out of nowhere.{w}The storm was shaped like a small doll and a bearded swordfighter.{w}
note: Source lacks the final [JP]; period added.

en: "GYAAAH!"{w}
note: Speaker ??? (Decoy, unseen yet).

en: "Waaait, Decoykiiins!"{w}
note: Speaker ??? (Milonya).

en: "Get away! Stay the hell away from me!{w}You... you Beard Girl!{w}Die! Die, or turn into a beard!"{w}
note: [JP] = "Beard Lady" (Decoy's insult; recurs in slice_15).

en:
"Aww, come on, Decoykins!
Call me by my proper name -- Milonya!"{w}

"GYAAAH!{w}I said quit comin' over here!
Get back! Don't touch me! Stop rubbin' up on meee!"{w}
note: [JP] = rubbing cheeks/body against someone affectionately.

en: "Decoykiiins!{w}Aaah! The way you run away is just so pretty-witty!!"{w}
note: [JP] (baby-talk "pretty") -> "pretty-witty".

en: "...SPURT! (nosebleed)"{w}
note: [JP] = spurting sound; stage direction [JP] kept in parentheses. Same line recurs in slice_15 rows 1139/1141.

en: The storm passed.{w}Left behind were copious bloodstains, suggesting some terrible tragedy,{w}{p}and yet,{w}the people who had seen the whole thing were going about their day as if nothing had happened.{w}{p}Apparently this was an everyday occurrence.{w}
note: The sentence runs across the page break in the source; cut at the same point.

en:
"Oh, excuse me!
Have you seen Decoykins?{w}...I'm sure Decoykins is around here somewhere..."{w}{p}"Who's Decoykins? Oh...
I'm sorry! I just assumed you were from this town.{w}Decoykins is cute and teeny-tiny and..."{w}{p}"...and the way Decoykins scampers around is just too cute!
Who knew something so pretty-witty existed in this world!{w}Aaah... I just can't help myself!{w}
note: No closing quote in source; kept. Decoy named instead of a pronoun (gender unknown). The second page answers an implied question from the party.

en: "Oh, it's the adventurers from the other day!{w}Decoykins ran off on me again...{w}If you see Decoykins, please let me know!"{w}
"...? My name? Like I said, it's Decoyki...?{w}
note: Speaker ????? = Milonya before being named; she starts to give Decoy's name instead of her own. No closing quote; repeated in next rows.

en:
{0E}"...? My name? Like I said, it's Decoyki...?{0F}
Oh, I'm so sorry! I was so wrapped up in Decoykins!{w}
"Beard Girl, more like!!"{w}
note: [JP] = "you mean Beard Lady".

en: Milonya
note: Source name box reads [JP] (a typo for [JP]); rendered with the glossary spelling Milonya.

en:
"Oh, found you, Decoykins!
Waaait! Let me snuggle all that fluff!"{w}
note: Speaker field shows the typo name [JP]; same character. [JP] = fluffy cuddling.
